limitations: Hot-cache standalone predicate/scan and 16-byte color-write model, common compact layout and traversal; not the full game roster or allocation path.
One selection scan means one query over one original corpus system, not one 222-definition global scan.
Call mixtures are explicitly constructed corpus workloads, not measured gameplay frequency. Tiny exact/family cases include hit and absent-query calls.
Includes common indirect call, changing-color generation, and returned hit-count accumulation overhead; output hashing is outside timing.
Unnamed stricmp and first-byte fast baselines are separate; nullptr-All already avoids string comparison.
Prefix baseline is preserved strlen guard plus strnicmp; cached-length strnicmp is reported separately for sensitivity.
FIND cases measure first-definition lookup only, including hit and miss; no particle spawn, crossfade duration calculation or fade execution.

Measures the same first-definition-table strategy used by exact CrossFade; allocation/execution excluded. Table is 113 ints per system definition (452 bytes), first declaration-order match; construction and invalidation are outside timing.

Runtime-instance unnamed and family selections still scan every live instance; the definition table cannot replace those operations. Timed model has one instance per definition; duplicate-instance semantics are validated separately.
FadeOut present-system case queries only the five 2-definition corpus systems containing FadeOut (first index 1); full-corpus FadeOut is a synthetic absence-heavy workload.
Single pinned local run under normal Windows scheduling; small ns differences may reflect noise, CPU frequency and background activity. No FPS claim.
